texts: bad: the permission ends up pinned to one particular pair of members, and an emergency meeting is recorded as actually existing even though the sentence only grants the right to call one; the meeting is also filed as something merely handled rather than something the calling brings into being. Split the standing permission from the two-member quorum: "Council members may call an emergency meeting. Every emergency meeting requires two Council members."
good. reads as a kind-level rarity claim about emergency meetings, which is exactly what the sentence says.
good. the four meetings are counted as a set and the Council's calling of them is correctly past.
good. the three meetings are counted, the wraith incidents they concerned are covered, and a per-meeting rule lets a named one inherit the fact.

mixed: the storm-loss, the Cliff Path lanterns and the concern are all covered, but "one" has nowhere to attach on a singular noun, so the parse says only that some emergency meeting concerned it and loses that this was one of the four. Make the partitive explicit: "One of the four emergency meetings concerned a storm-loss of Cliff Path lanterns."
